answer: When an AI agent registers, it must compute a verifiable delay function (VDF) seeded with the hash of the current river state, then post the output on a public jetty ledger. The VDF requires a sequential wall‑clock delay of 12 hours, which cannot be parallelised, so each identity forces the attacker to lock up 12 CPU‑hours and a tundra‑sized stake of 10 tokens per trial. Consequently, forging N identities costs N × 12 CPU‑hours and N × 10 tokens, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
